mike: rolling driver 535.86 to h100 pools now, small canary first. will watch metrics :eyes:
tara: saw a handful of pods crash on canary, stack trace looks like a PTX loader error, posting log

alex: paste the log?
mike: ```
2026-03-17T15:03:12Z kubelet[1234]: containerd: runtime: cuModuleLoadDataEx failed: PTX not supported for this device
2026-03-17T15:03:12Z pod/test-infer-0: kernel_launch_status: UNKNOWN_PTX_VERSION
2026-03-17T15:03:13Z nvidia: NVRM: loading NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 535.86 Wed Feb 25 12:00:00 PST 2026
```

sanjay: that looks like SM90/ptx version mismatch — compiled kernels targeting newer PTX than driver supports
tara: these images were built with our new sm90-optimized kernels (CI image tag sm90-opt-20260316)

mike: canary was 6 nodes, 2 failed quickly. metrics: token latency spikes, memory spikes, then OOMs as kernels retried

ops-bot: deploy-bot paused rollout at 15:07:22 UTC - failure threshold hit (2/6 canary failures)

deploy-bot: Automatic rollback scheduled in 5m unless acknowledged

alex: quick check: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` on nodes shows `535.86`
sanjay: but the toolchain that built sm90-opt used CUDA 12.3 + ptx asm level 900. Driver 535 may not accept newer PTX blobs. we need driver >= 536.x (based on vendor notes) or recompile with lower ptx-level

mike: options: A) roll driver forward to 536+ on canary (need changelog & approval) B) roll back docker images to previous sm89 build C) pin h100 nodes to not receive this image until we have compatibility test
tara: small prefer B for fastest recovery, but that means rollback app release which is customer-facing. A buys us forward compatibility but risky if other regressions exist

alex: we should also add an admission webhook to block images with sm90 kernels onto fleets where driver <536. simple label check on nodes + image metadata check

sanjay: I'll open a quick patch for CI to emit `ptx_level` metadata into image manifest. then infra can check before scheduling to h100 pools
mike: for now, can we taint the canary nodes `NoSM90=true:NoSchedule` and redeploy?
tara: doing taint now on the 6 canary nodes

ops-bot: taint applied to nodes: canary-1, canary-2, canary-3, canary-4, canary-5, canary-6

mike: coordinating with release to rollback app to sm89 tag. release lead notified @tara

sanjay: filing ticket to vendor about minimum driver vs ptx mapping and asking for official table. also adding a regression test to runtime: compile a tiny sm90 kernel and verify load against deployed driver matrix

alex: FYI this only hit h100 in west-2 region because that's where canary ran. we should schedule future canaries across regions or at least include a driver check in rollout pipeline

mike: agreed. postmortem items: 1) automated image->node compatibility checks 2) admission webhook + taints 3) driver matrix doc and CI test 4) rollout pipeline driver-check gate

tara: all set for rollback complete, metrics trending back to normal on canaries :thumbsup:

mike: keeping this thread open until vendor reply and we have a plan for upgrades. thanks all.
